author: Jason Olson
title: Vavorsky steps down from Kennedy wrestling after 46 years - NewsBreak
text:
By Jason Olson ,
16 hours ago
When people think of Bloomington Kennedy High School wrestling, the first thing that comes to mind is head coach Chuck Vavrosky. It’s a well-deserved recognition for a proud program graduate who resigned on Thursday, June 4, after 46 years at the helm.
Vavrosky confirmed he will not return to the program next winter, marking the first time he will not coach the Eagles since 1980, when reached by phone on Monday, June 8. He declined to discuss the reason for his resignation, and a message to Bloomington Public Schools Communications Executive Director Rick Kaufman confirmed that Vavrosky resigned as coach but plans to continue to teach at Kennedy this upcoming school year.
Vavorsky has a 489-406 career record, good for the 19th most wins by a Minnesota coach. He started with a 5-63 record over the first three seasons to coach 136 state entrants, 35 state placewinners and 15 state champions. In the team format, his best finish was third place in 2009, despite competing in the same section as the dynasty at Apple Valley. “We were ranked ninth in the country at the time and they were third,” Vavorsky explained.
Vavorsky and Dave Ahrens are the only head coaches the program has known, combining for 26 state individual wrestling championships which ranks 14th for the most titles. Ahrens coached 11 state champions, including Vavorsky who was a runner-up as a junior before finishing out his senior season with the state championship. He went on win a Cadet world title along with nine national titles.
The branches on the Vavorsky coaching tress run as deep as the roots of a Sequoia, not just a 300-year-old Oak. The list includes Joel Sharratt who coached at the Naval Academy as an assistant coach from 2000-2006 and head coach from 2014-20 and head coach at the Air Force Academy from 2006-14. An NCAA Champion in 1994, Sharratt was a three-time NCAA finalist and All-American and was a two-time captain with the University of Iowa.
The Morgan brothers, Marty, John and Gordy Morgan, combined to earn nine collegiate All-American honors with the University of Minnesota and 10 national Greco-Roman titles. John wrestled in the 1988 Seoul Olympics and Gordy in the 1996 Atlanta Olympics. Marty won a national title at 177 pounds in 1991 with a perfect 39-0 season as a senior. He returned to coach with J Robinson from 1996-2008.
Jayson and Dylan Ness are more lifelong successful wrestlers to develop their wrestling careers at Kennedy before winning state high school titles and beyond to NCAA, national and international success with the University of Minnesota and beyond. Jayson Ness wrestled for the Gophers from 2006-10 earning a 31-0 senior season with an NCAA title in 2010 to win the Dan Hodge Trophy. Dylan wrestled for the Gophers from 2011-15 earning four All-American honors reaching the NCAA finals twice in 2012 (149 pounds) and 2014 (157 pounds). He was voted Mr. Minnesota High School Wrestler in 2010.
For many years, the coaching staff was comprised of former Eagles wrestlers and many have gone on to coach their own high school or youth level programs, too many to count.
Vavorsky plans to teach one more year in 2026-27.
